Array two-pointer passes require either sorted data or monotonic directionality to guarantee O(n) convergence without missing pairs.
Sliding window algorithms must maintain loop invariants: expand the right pointer to include elements, and contract the left pointer while window constraints are violated.
Hash map indexing replaces nested loops with O(1) lookup, trading O(n) auxiliary space for O(n) total runtime.
Binary search requires calculating midpoints using left + (right - left) // 2 to avoid overflow and strictly defining search range invariants [left, right] vs [left, right).
Monotonic stacks preserve elements in strictly increasing or decreasing order, resolving next-greater or nearest-boundary problems in amortized O(n) time.
Graph and grid BFS traversal guarantees shortest path in unweighted graphs when visited nodes are marked immediately upon queue insertion to prevent duplicate enqueueing.
